Method One: Eat Meat
Start each morning with a hearty meal of Meat, accompanied by two Bowls of porridge. Be sure to avoid cold porridge, as it will cause thunderous stomach growls and undo all your progress.

Method Two: Bone Forging
Swing the hammer daily from dawn until three quarters past the morning hour. Begin by lifting light weights as if they were heavy, then progress to lifting heavy weights as if they were light.

Method Three: Rest and Purification
Muscles are like dough—they need time to rest after kneading. Therefore, take one day off every seven days. Boil mugwort for a cleansing bath and use bamboo cups to remove stagnant energy.

Method Four: Stance Training
Find a large tree and assume a horse stance beneath it. Gradually increase your endurance from one hundred breaths to a thousand. Only when your legs tremble like sieves and sweat pours like a spring will you grasp its essence.

Method Five: Naked Running
At the crow of the rooster, run naked in the wild, mimicking the leap of a fierce tiger and the pounce of a hungry Wolf. Be careful to avoid vegetable patches—trampling them will cost you Coin.

Method Six: Tendon Tempering
Practice bare-chested in the snowy fields during winter and carry stones under the midday sun in summer. At first, your muscles will feel as if pricked by needles, then scorched by fire, until warmth surges from your core.

Method Seven: Qi Cultivation
Sit cross-legged by the riverbank at dusk, observing the flow of water to guide your breath. Silently recite the mantra, "Qi sinks to the bubbling spring, strength reaches the fingertips," until your entire body is at peace.

These seven methods require no silver, but three things are indispensable: the relentless drive to rise before dawn, the obsession to train in the summer heat, and the foolish persistence to endure the winter's Sanjiu. If you diligently follow these methods, within three months, your muscles will rival those of a plowing ox. Fellow practitioners, let us strive together!
